title: Joshua Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 1.

questions.question: Who spoke to Joshua after the death of Moses?
options: The LORD
Moses' spirit
Aaron
The elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:1 states that the LORD spake unto Joshua after the death of Moses.

questions.question: What was Joshua commanded to do after Moses died?
options: Arise and go over the Jordan with all the people
Build an altar
Remain in the wilderness
Send spies into the land
questions.correctAnswer: Arise and go over the Jordan with all the people
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:2 commands Joshua to arise and go over the Jordan with all the people to the land given to Israel.

questions.question: To whom did the LORD say He was giving the land?
options: The children of Israel
The Hittites
The Egyptians
The Amorites
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:2 clearly states the land is given to the children of Israel.

questions.question: What did the LORD say about every place the sole of Joshua's foot would tread upon?
options: It was given to him
It was forbidden
It was cursed
It was unknown territory
questions.correctAnswer: It was given to him
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:3 says every place that the sole of Joshua's foot shall tread upon is given to him.

questions.question: Which river was mentioned as a boundary of the land given to Israel?
options: The river Euphrates
The Nile
The Tigris
The Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: The river Euphrates
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:4 mentions the great river, the river Euphrates, as a boundary of the land.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised Joshua that no man would be able to stand before him all the days of his life.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:5 states that no man shall be able to stand before Joshua all his life.

questions.question: How did the LORD say He would be with Joshua compared to Moses?
options: The LORD will be with Joshua as He was with Moses
The LORD will be less present with Joshua
The LORD will only guide Moses' spirit
The LORD will not be with Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will be with Joshua as He was with Moses
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:5 states the LORD will be with Joshua as He was with Moses.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD said He would fail and forsake Joshua.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:5 explicitly says the LORD will not fail nor forsake Joshua.

questions.question: What two qualities did the LORD command Joshua to have?
options: Be strong and of good courage
Be humble and silent
Be patient and meek
Be wise and wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and of good courage
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:6 commands Joshua to be strong and of good courage.

questions.question: Who was Joshua to divide the land to?
options: The people of Israel
The Egyptians
The Philistines
The Moabites
questions.correctAnswer: The people of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:6 says Joshua shall divide the land as an inheritance to the people.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD swore to give the land to the fathers of the people Joshua would lead.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:6 mentions the land which the LORD swore unto their fathers to give them.

questions.question: In Joshua 1, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Arise and go over the Jordan
Be strong and of good courage
Divide the land as an inheritance
Meditate on the law day and night
questions.correctAnswer: Arise and go over the Jordan
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:2 gives the command to arise and go over the Jordan before other instructions.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua was told to be afraid and dismayed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:9 commands Joshua not to be afraid or dismayed.

questions.question: Who was Joshua described as in relation to Moses?
options: Moses' minister
Moses' brother
Moses' father
Moses' enemy
questions.correctAnswer: Moses' minister
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:1 calls Joshua the son of Nun and Moses' minister.

questions.question: What was the extent of the land promised to Joshua according to the LORD?
options: From the wilderness and Lebanon to the Euphrates and the great sea
From Egypt to Babylon
From the Red Sea to the Dead Sea
From the Jordan to the Mediterranean Sea only
questions.correctAnswer: From the wilderness and Lebanon to the Euphrates and the great sea
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:4 describes the land from the wilderness and Lebanon unto the Euphrates and the great sea.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Joshua 1:7, what is necessary for Joshua to prosper wherever he goes?
options: Be strong and very courageous, and observe to do all the law given by Moses
Lead the people with kindness and generosity
Build altars throughout the land
Gather an army from the surrounding tribes
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and very courageous, and observe to do all the law given by Moses
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:7 instructs Joshua to be strong and very courageous and to carefully obey all the law Moses commanded so that he may prosper wherever he goes. This emphasizes the need for courage and obedience to God's law as prerequisites for success (Joshua 1:7, Joshua 1:8, Joshua 1:9).

questions.question: What does Joshua 1:8 say will happen if the book of the law is meditated on day and night and obeyed?
options: Your way will be prosperous and you will have good success
You will become the richest among the people
You will never face any enemies
You will receive immediate answers to prayers
questions.correctAnswer: Your way will be prosperous and you will have good success
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:8 clearly states that meditating on the law day and night and observing it leads to a prosperous way and good success. This links faithful study and obedience to tangible blessings (Joshua 1:7, Joshua 1:8, Joshua 1:9).

questions.question: In Joshua 1:9, why does God command Joshua to be strong and courageous and not afraid or dismayed?
options: Because the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest
Because Joshua will fight all battles alone
Because the people are fully prepared
Because the enemy will surrender immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:9 reassures Joshua that God’s presence accompanies him wherever he goes, serving as the basis for strength and courage without fear or dismay. This connects God's presence to Joshua's confidence (Joshua 1:7, Joshua 1:8, Joshua 1:9).

questions.question: What specific command did Joshua give to the officers of the people in Joshua 1:10?
options: Pass through the host and command the people to prepare victuals
Build a sanctuary before crossing the Jordan
Choose twelve men to spy on the land
Gather stones to create a memorial
questions.correctAnswer: Pass through the host and command the people to prepare victuals
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:10 records Joshua’s order to the officers to command the people to prepare food supplies because they would cross the Jordan in three days to possess the promised land. This shows practical preparation for obedience (Joshua 1:10, Joshua 1:11, Joshua 1:12).

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'three days' mentioned in Joshua 1:11 in relation to the people's journey?
options: They will cross the Jordan within three days to possess the land
They will rest for three days before traveling
They will wait three days for Moses’ instructions
They will fight battles for three days
questions.correctAnswer: They will cross the Jordan within three days to possess the land
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:11 highlights the urgency and promise that within three days the Israelites will cross the Jordan River to take possession of the land God has given them, indicating faith and readiness (Joshua 1:10, Joshua 1:11).

questions.question: How does Joshua 1:12 describe the role of the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh during the conquest?
options: They are to support their brethren by leading armed before them
They are to remain in their land and not participate
They are to build fortifications on their side of the Jordan
They are to send offerings to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: They are to support their brethren by leading armed before them
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:12 explains that these tribes, although settled on the east side of Jordan, are to help their brethren by crossing armed ahead of them to support in the conquest, demonstrating unity and cooperation (Joshua 1:12, Joshua 1:14).

questions.question: What instruction did Moses give to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, as Joshua reminds them in Joshua 1:13?
options: That the LORD has given them rest and this land
To build an altar as a memorial
To prepare for battle without fear
To separate themselves from the other tribes
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD has given them rest and this land
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:13 reminds these tribes that Moses commanded them to remember that God had granted them rest and possession of the land on their side of the Jordan, affirming God’s faithfulness and rest after labor (Joshua 1:12, Joshua 1:13).

questions.question: According to Joshua 1:14, where were the wives, children, and cattle of these tribes to remain during the conquest?
options: In the land Moses gave them on this side of the Jordan
Crossing the Jordan alongside the warriors
In the wilderness for safety
In the cities of the Hittites
questions.correctAnswer: In the land Moses gave them on this side of the Jordan
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:14 specifies that the families and cattle of these tribes were to stay safely in the land Moses had already given them east of the Jordan, while the warriors went ahead to help their brethren, showing a division of responsibilities (Joshua 1:12, Joshua 1:14).

questions.question: What was the condition mentioned in Joshua 1:15 for the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh to return to their own land?
options: After the LORD had given their brethren rest and they had possessed their land
After the first harvest in the promised land
After the building of the altar at Jordan
After three years of service in battle
questions.correctAnswer: After the LORD had given their brethren rest and they had possessed their land
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:15 states that these tribes were to remain with their brethren until God gave the rest to their brethren and they possessed their land, after which they could return to their own inheritance, emphasizing patience and unity (Joshua 1:14, Joshua 1:15).

questions.question: How did the people respond to Joshua's commands in Joshua 1:16?
options: They promised to obey all his commands and follow wherever he sent them
They refused to follow until Moses returned
They requested more time to prepare
They asked for signs from God first
questions.correctAnswer: They promised to obey all his commands and follow wherever he sent them
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:16 records the people's full commitment to obey Joshua’s commands and follow his leadership wherever he sends them, showing faith and continuity in leadership (Joshua 1:16, Joshua 1:17).

questions.question: What comparison do the people make between Joshua and Moses in Joshua 1:17?
options: They will obey Joshua as they obeyed Moses, trusting God to be with him as He was with Moses
They believe Joshua is not as capable as Moses
They fear Joshua will not lead them well
They request that Joshua perform miracles like Moses
questions.correctAnswer: They will obey Joshua as they obeyed Moses, trusting God to be with him as He was with Moses
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:17 shows the people's faithfulness in promising to obey Joshua just as they obeyed Moses, while also praying that God's presence would be with Joshua as it was with Moses, emphasizing leadership continuity and trust in God (Joshua 1:16, Joshua 1:17).

questions.question: According to Joshua 1:18, what consequence is given for anyone who rebels against Joshua's commandment?
options: He shall be put to death
He shall be exiled from the camp
He shall be publicly rebuked
He shall be forgiven after repentance
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be put to death
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:18 clearly states that anyone who rebels and refuses to obey Joshua’s commands shall be put to death, underscoring the seriousness of obedience to God’s appointed leader (Joshua 1:18).

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 1:8 teaches that meditating on the book of the law day and night ensures that the reader will have good success.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:8 explicitly states that meditating on the law day and night and observing it leads to a prosperous way and good success, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 1:14 commands the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh to leave their families and cattle behind and cross the Jordan with the rest of the Israelites.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:14 states that the wives, little ones, and cattle of these tribes shall remain in the land Moses gave them on this side of the Jordan, while the armed men pass before their brethren, proving the statement false.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 1:9, the reason Joshua should not be afraid is because the LORD thy God is with him wherever he goes.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:9 commands Joshua to be strong and courageous without fear or dismay because God is with him wherever he goes, confirming the statement as true.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to Joshua 1:13, what did Moses command the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh to remember?
options: The LORD your God hath given you rest, and hath given you this land
To prepare victuals for the journey
To obey Joshua in all things
To build an altar on this side of Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD your God hath given you rest, and hath given you this land
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:13 explicitly states that Moses commanded them to remember that the LORD their God has given them rest and this land.

questions.question: Who were to remain in the land given on this side of Jordan while the mighty men crossed over to help their brethren, according to Joshua 1:14?
options: Wives, little ones, and cattle
Elders and priests
All the people
Only the warriors
questions.correctAnswer: Wives, little ones, and cattle
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:14 states that wives, little ones, and cattle would remain in the land given on this side of Jordan, while the armed men passed before their brethren.

questions.question: What was the condition for the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh to return to their own land, according to Joshua 1:15?
options: After the LORD has given their brethren rest and they have possessed the land
After a specified number of years
Once they build a temple
When Joshua commands them to return
questions.correctAnswer: After the LORD has given their brethren rest and they have possessed the land
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:15 makes clear they would return only after the LORD had given their brethren rest and they possessed the land given to them.

questions.question: How did the people respond to Joshua's commands in Joshua 1:16?
options: All that thou commandest us we will do, and whithersoever thou sendest us, we will go
They expressed doubt and hesitation
They requested more time to prepare
They asked for a sign from God
questions.correctAnswer: All that thou commandest us we will do, and whithersoever thou sendest us, we will go
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:16 records their full commitment to obey Joshua and go wherever he sends them.

questions.question: What comparison is made regarding the people's obedience to Joshua in Joshua 1:17?
options: As we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee
We will obey only if God commands it
We will obey partially as before
Our obedience will depend on the success in battle
questions.correctAnswer: As we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:17 shows a direct parallel of obedience to Joshua as they had to Moses, contingent on God’s presence with Joshua.

questions.question: What consequence is given for rebellion against Joshua's command in Joshua 1:18?
options: He shall be put to death
He shall be exiled
He shall be publicly reprimanded
He shall be forgiven after repentance
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be put to death
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:18 clearly states that any rebel who disobeys Joshua’s commands shall be put to death.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'courage' in Joshua 1:9 imply in the original language context?
options: Strength to endure and face challenges boldly
Physical power only
Emotional happiness
Avoidance of fear through ignorance
questions.correctAnswer: Strength to endure and face challenges boldly
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chazaq' used here means to be strong, firm, or courageous, implying a resolute strength to endure and act boldly.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the promise of God being with His servant as stated in Joshua 1:5?
options: Exodus 33:14
Genesis 12:2
Psalms 23:4
Isaiah 41:10
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 33:14
questions.explanation: Exodus 33:14 promises God's presence with Moses, echoing the assurance given to Joshua in Joshua 1:5 that God will be with him as He was with Moses.

questions.question: In Joshua 1:8, what is the purpose of meditating on the Book of the Law day and night?
options: That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein and prosper
To memorize it for public reading
To debate with others about it
To prepare sacrifices accordingly
questions.correctAnswer: That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein and prosper
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:8 states meditation on the law leads to obedience and results in prosperity and success.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Joshua 1:9 with the phrases 'Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed'?
options: Parallelism
Chiasm
Allegory
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:9 uses synonymous parallelism, repeating the encouragement to be strong and courageous while forbidding fear and dismay.

questions.question: Joshua 1:11 commands the people to prepare victuals for crossing the Jordan within how many days?
options: Three days
Seven days
One day
Ten days
questions.correctAnswer: Three days
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:11 instructs the people to prepare food supplies as they will cross the Jordan in three days.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 1:16 indicates that the people were hesitant and unwilling to follow Joshua's commands.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:16 shows the people’s full willingness and obedience to Joshua’s commands, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 1:5 promises that no man will be able to stand before Joshua all the days of his life.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:5 explicitly states that no man shall be able to stand before Joshua all his life, affirming God’s protection.

questions.question: Joshua 1:7 emphasizes that Joshua should not turn to the right or left but observe all the law given by Moses. This theme is echoed in which New Testament passage?
options: James 1:25
Romans 8:1
Hebrews 12:2
1 Corinthians 13:4
questions.correctAnswer: James 1:25
questions.explanation: James 1:25 encourages believers to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein, echoing Joshua's exhortation to observe all the law without turning aside.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'until the LORD have given your brethren rest' in Joshua 1:15 in terms of the historical context of Israel's conquest?
options: It indicates the ongoing conquest was not complete until God granted rest to all tribes
It suggests a permanent division between tribes
It refers to a Sabbath rest every seventh year
It signals the building of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates the ongoing conquest was not complete until God granted rest to all tribes
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:15 shows that the conquest and settling were progressive; rest was given by God only after possession of land was complete for each tribe.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in God's promise to Joshua that 'I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee'?
options: Omnipresence
Omniscience
Immutability
Faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:5 shows God's promise to Joshua that He will not fail or forsake him, which reveals God's faithfulness to His covenant and His people.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about sanctification is emphasized by the command to 'meditate therein day and night' on the book of the law?
options: Sanctification requires continual engagement with God's Word
Sanctification is achieved by human effort alone
Sanctification is only external obedience
Sanctification is irrelevant to leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification requires continual engagement with God's Word
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:8 instructs Joshua to meditate day and night on the law to observe it, highlighting that sanctification involves ongoing reflection and obedience to God's Word.

questions.question: How does Joshua 1:2–4 contribute to the biblical narrative of God’s covenantal promises?
options: It affirms the territorial fulfillment of the Abrahamic covenant
It introduces a new covenant replacing the old one
It denies the promise of land to Israel
It focuses on the temple worship exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms the territorial fulfillment of the Abrahamic covenant
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:2-4 recounts God's command to Joshua to lead Israel into the land He promised, which aligns with the Abrahamic covenant's promise of land to Israel.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by God's assurance to Joshua that 'there shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life'?
options: Divine sovereignty over enemies
Human free will as ultimate power
Predestination to failure
Salvation by works
questions.correctAnswer: Divine sovereignty over enemies
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:5 reveals God's sovereign protection over Joshua, indicating that no enemy can stand before him due to God's power, not human ability.

questions.question: What theological insight arises from combining the commands of Joshua 1:7 and Joshua 1:8 about obedience and meditation on the law?
options: Obedience rooted in meditation leads to prosperity and success
Meditation on the law is optional for success
Obedience without meditation is superior
Prosperity is unrelated to God's law
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience rooted in meditation leads to prosperity and success
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:7 commands strong courage to obey the law, while 1:8 links meditating on the law with prosperity, teaching that obedience grounded in continual reflection leads to blessing.

questions.question: How does Joshua 1:9 emphasize the attribute of God that is essential for courage in leadership?
options: God’s presence with His people wherever they go
God’s wrath against enemies
God’s silence in times of trial
God’s judgment on disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence with His people wherever they go
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:9 commands courage because the LORD God is with Joshua wherever he goes, emphasizing God's omnipresence as the source of fearless leadership.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of Joshua instructing the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh to assist the other tribes before enjoying their own inheritance (Joshua 1:14-15)?
options: It illustrates communal responsibility within God's covenant people
It highlights tribal independence over unity
It suggests partial exclusion from the land
It prioritizes personal possession over collective mission
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates communal responsibility within God's covenant people
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:14-15 teaches that these tribes must help their brethren gain rest and possession before returning to enjoy their own land, showing mutual covenantal support and unity.

questions.question: According to Joshua 1:16–17, what principle regarding leadership succession and obedience is taught?
options: Obedience to Joshua is modeled after obedience to Moses
Obedience to Joshua is optional
Moses’ leadership is rejected
Leadership is based on popularity
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to Joshua is modeled after obedience to Moses
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:16-17 shows the people's commitment to obey Joshua as they did Moses, emphasizing continuity and divine authority in leadership succession.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about divine guidance and human responsibility is found in Joshua 1:6 and Joshua 1:11?
options: God commands courage and requires preparation for His promises
God’s promises remove all human responsibility
Human effort alone secures the land
Divine commands are symbolic only
questions.correctAnswer: God commands courage and requires preparation for His promises
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:6 urges courage to divide the land promised by God, while 1:11 commands practical preparation to cross the Jordan, teaching cooperation of divine command and human action.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by His promise 'as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee' in Joshua 1:5?
options: God’s faithfulness and unchanging nature
God’s wrath
God’s hiddenness
God’s silence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness and unchanging nature
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:5 shows God’s faithfulness by assuring Joshua that His presence with Moses will be the same with Joshua, indicating God’s immutability.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine promises in Joshua 1 are merely symbolic and not meant to be taken literally. What does Joshua 1:2-4 actually teach about God's promises?
options: God’s promises are concrete and territorial, specifying actual land boundaries
God’s promises are vague and non-specific
God’s promises were eventually revoked
God’s promises only apply spiritually, not physically
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promises are concrete and territorial, specifying actual land boundaries
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:2-4 clearly defines the land borders God promises to Israel, showing the literal and concrete nature of His covenant promises against sceptical claims.

questions.question: What theological theme emerges from Joshua's command in 1:18 concerning rebellion against his leadership?
options: The seriousness of covenantal obedience under God-ordained leadership
The irrelevance of leadership in God’s plan
The acceptance of rebellion as permissible
The importance of individual autonomy over God's commands
questions.correctAnswer: The seriousness of covenantal obedience under God-ordained leadership
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:18 states that rebels against Joshua’s commands shall be put to death, underscoring the gravity of disobedience within God's covenant community.

questions.question: How does Joshua 1:13 reveal God's provision and rest for His people in the context of covenant theology?
options: God has given rest and land to His people as fulfillment of His promises
God withholds rest until the end of the age
Rest is unrelated to God's covenant
Land is earned by human merit alone
questions.correctAnswer: God has given rest and land to His people as fulfillment of His promises
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:13 recalls Moses' word that the LORD has given rest and land, showing God's faithfulness in covenant fulfillment by providing His people with rest and inheritance.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal understanding about God's presence and human courage can be drawn from Joshua 1:9 and Joshua 1:7?
options: God’s presence empowers human courage to obey and succeed
Human courage is sufficient without God’s presence
Fear and dismay are encouraged
Obedience is unrelated to courage
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence empowers human courage to obey and succeed
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:7 calls for strength and courage to obey the law, and 1:9 reassures that God’s presence enables this courage, connecting divine support with human responsibility.

questions.question: What does Joshua 1:3 teach about God's sovereignty and promise regarding the land?
options: God sovereignly gives every place the foot treads upon to His people
The land is given based on Israel’s military strength alone
The land is only a temporary possession
God’s promise is conditional on sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly gives every place the foot treads upon to His people
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:3 affirms God's sovereign gift of every place Joshua’s foot shall tread, indicating divine authority over the land promised to Israel.
